author_bio: Mouli Sharma is a journalist, freelance illustrator, and writer from New Delhi, India. She is a published photojournalist & illustrator, having been featured in The Hindu College Gazette, & the quarterly Pink Disco. Mouli took over as the Editor of The Voice Express (https://thevoiceexpress.github.io/e-mag/) back in September 2023.
content:
The following press note was released by the civil society solidarity group that had organised a silent demonstration against the Indian government's complicity in Israel's genocide in and of occupied Palestine at Delhi's Nehru Place on the 29th of July 2025. The group, consisting various student organisations including AISA, SFI, etc, along with Palestine Advocacy groups such as Indians for Palestine, and civil society members like economist Jean Drèze, automobile worker rights leader Khushiram, former DU Teacher's Association President Nandita Narain, former IAS officer Harsh Mander and many more, faced mob violence and threats of police detention.

New Delhi, July 19, 2025: A peaceful demonstration in solidarity with the people of Palestine was held this afternoon in Nehru Place, one of the capital’s busiest commercial districts. Organised by a broad coalition of citizens and organisations, including students, academics, artists, and activists, the flash protest was intended as a non-violent, public expression of solidarity with Gaza and a denunciation of Israel’s genocidal war. About a hundred participants gathered around 12:30 PM. They carried Palestinian flags, posters, and placards with messages such as “Free Palestine,” “Stop the Genocide,” and “Ceasefire Now.” Leaflets and stickers were distributed to passersby, sparking conversations and awareness around the humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in Gaza.

The gathering also served to condemn the Indian government’s ongoing complicity in Israel’s campaign. Over the past two years, more than 50,000 people, mostly civilians, have been killed in Gaza. Thousands more are injured, displaced, starving, and denied medical care. Israel’s war has been systematic, deliberate, and documented live. Yet the Indian government has not only remained silent, but actively participated, subsidising defence-sector joint ventures, dispatching Indian workers to replace Palestinian labour in Israel, and repeatedly abstaining from UN resolutions that condemn Israel’s crimes.

Despite the strictly peaceful nature of the demonstration, it was met with hostility from many local onlookers and passers-by. A large and hostile crowd quickly surrounded the protestors. Some individuals from the mob approached protestors and questioned their motives, asking, “Why don’t you raise the Indian flag too?” In an effort to engage peacefully, one demonstrator did raise the Indian flag. However, it was quickly snatched away, and the crowd began chanting “Bharat Mata ki Jai”; some also chanted “Jai Shri Ram.” From that point, the mob’s behaviour became increasingly aggressive.

Water and mud were hurled at protestors from balconies above. Some chanted “Israel Zindabad, Palestine Murdabad,” turning the space into a site of hostility and intimidation. Eyewitness accounts describe rapid escalation and targeted harassment, particularly of Muslim participants and women protestors. One demonstrator shared: “It went really south… A Sanghi crowd formed instantly and began aggressive sloganeering. They cornered our Muslim colleague and started harassing women. I saw men surrounding a female participant and shouting at her.”

“It went really south… A Sanghi crowd formed instantly and began aggressive
sloganeering. They cornered our Muslim colleague and started harassing women.
I saw men surrounding a female participant and shouting at her.” - A demonstrator at Nehru Place on 19th July 2025.

The police eventually arrived, but rather than addressing the aggression of the right-wing crowd, they demanded permission papers from the protestors. No action was taken against those who had disrupted the event, hurled objects, or threatened participants. This selective enforcement only reinforced what many already know: the right to peaceful assembly and dissent is under severe attack in today’s India, while impunity is often extended to those aligned with majoritarian power.

The choice of Nehru Place as a site was symbolic, an open, public market square frequented by working-class people, students, and office-goers alike. It was meant to reclaim democratic space in a city where protest is now virtually criminalised. Despite everything, the message of the gathering remains clear: There are Indians who stand, and will continue to stand, with the people of Palestine.

Press note by19th July collective. For further information or interviews, please contact: Anjali (8130580438), Aban (9711155641), Priya (9311548645).

related.excerpt: Thousands of current and former non-permanent Maruti-Suzuki workers gathered at the Gurgaon DC office on 10th January 2025 to submit their charter of demands, challenging the company's hire-and-fire labour practices and demanding equal pay and permanent employment alongside the already-protesting terminated workers.
related.title: “Not Your Footballs!” Newly Formed Union of Non-Permanent Maruti-Suzuki Employees Intensifies Agitation, Calls Out Abuse of Contract Workers

related.excerpt: The official press release of the Maruti Suzuki Asthayi Mazdoor Sangh, founded on 5th January 2025 in a mass meeting of over three thousand non-permanent workers at Gurgaon, announcing the union's formation, its charter of demands, and its solidarity with the already-protesting terminated workers.
related.title: 'Equal Work, Equal Pay': 'Temporary' Maruti-Suzuki Workers Establish Union, Join Hands With Protesting Terminated Workers

related.excerpt: COLLECTIVE Delhi's General Secretary Sourya's full statement on the posthumous veneration of Ratan N. Tata, challenging the media narrative of ethical entrepreneurship with a record of the Tata Group's land acquisitions, displacement of communities, and the selective memory that public mourning makes both possible and convenient.
related.title: Fickle Grief: COLLECTIVE Delhi Secretary Sourya’s Full Statement Against the Posthumous Veneration of Ratan N. Tata

related.excerpt: On 8th September 2025, India and Israel's finance ministers signed a Bilateral Investment Agreement in New Delhi. Forty-three organisations and forty-seven individuals released an open letter calling on India to withdraw from the treaty, calling it a material contribution to an ongoing genocide in Gaza.
related.title: 'Matters of Money': 43 Organisations Demand India's Withdrawal From Bilateral Investment Agreement with Israel Amidst Ongoing Genocide In Gaza

related.excerpt: A report on a practice documented in the occupied West Bank, where soldiers from Israeli settlements use laser sights from sniper rifles to play 'statue' with Palestinian families, forcing people to freeze on command. On the mundane, psychological texture of long-term military occupation.
related.title: "It's Okay, They're Just Playing With Us": Games of the Gun from the Occupied West Bank

related.excerpt: A photo essay from International Women's Day, 8th March 2026, at Jantar Mantar, where women from six to sixty gathered to protest the BJP government's neglect of women's safety and welfare, express solidarity with the women of Palestine and Iran, and raise demands for dignity, health, and work.
related.title: Bengal Remembers: Sengar, Epstein, and RG Kar's Legacy on International Women's Day in 2026
